title: Ensure 'Restrict ActiveX Install' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting enables blocking of ActiveX® control installation prompts for Internet Explorer processes. Users often choose to install software such as ActiveX controls that are not permitted by their organization's security policy. Such software can pose significant security and privacy risks to networks. Rationale: Microsoft ActiveX controls allow unmanaged, unprotected code to run on the user computers. ActiveX controls do not run within a protected container in the browser like other types of HTML or Microsoft Silverlight-based controls. 'Enabled: check all applications' writes one REG_DWORD 1 per Office executable under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Main\FeatureControl\FEATURE_RESTRICT_ACTIVEXINSTALL; the audit requires all 14 executables the ADMX writes (groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spdesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onenote.exe, mse7.exe) to be 1 and lists any that are missing or different.

title: Ensure 'Allow Trusted Locations on the network' is set to 'Disabled'
description: This policy setting controls whether trusted locations on the network can be used. Trusted locations specified in the Trust Center are used to define file locations that are assumed to be safe by the application opening the file. The recommended state for this setting is: Disabled. Rationale: Content, code, and add-ins are allowed to load from trusted locations with a minimal amount of security, without prompting the users for permission. User setting: the audit checks HKEY_USERS\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\access\security\trustedlocations:allownetworklocations (REG_DWORD) in every loaded user hive (S-1-5-21-*) and is compliant when each holds 0. It prints 'no-user-hive-loaded' (FAIL) when no user profile is loaded, so scan while users are logged on.
reference: CIS Microsoft Office Enterprise Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.1.1.3.2.1.1 Ensure 'Allow Trusted Locations on the network' is set to 'Disabled'

audit.command: $sids = @(Get-ChildItem -Path 'Registry::HKEY_USERS' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -match '^S-1-5-21-\d+-\d+-\d+-\d+$' } | ForEach-Object { $_.PSChildName }); if ($sids.Count -eq 0) { 'no-user-hive-loaded' } else { $bad = @(); foreach ($s in $sids) { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path ('Registry::HKEY_USERS\' + $s + '\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\access\security\trustedlocations') -Name 'allownetworklocations' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'allownetworklocations'; if (-not ($null -ne $v -and @(0) -contains [int64]$v)) { $bad += $s + ':allownetworklocations=' + $v } }; if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'non-compliant: ' + ($bad -join ', ') } }

remediation.guidance: Configure through Group Policy (User Configuration): User Configuration\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Access 2016\Application Settings\Security\Trust Center\Trusted Locations\Allow Trusted Locations on the network = Disabled

title: Ensure 'Block macros from running in Office files from the internet' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting allows the blocking of macros from running in Office files that come from the internet. By enabling this policy setting, macros are blocked from running, even if "Enable all macros" is selected in the Macro Settings section of the Trust Center. Users will receive a notification that macros are blocked from running. Rationale: Windows marks files downloaded from the internet using an alternate NTFS data stream. Files from untrusted sources can contain malicious payloads embedded in macros that may compromise the system on which they are run. Open/Save blocked, use open policy: Both opening and saving of the file type will be blocked. The file will open based on the policy setting configured in the "default file block behavior" key. Rationale: Using legacy file formats could allow malicious code to become active on user computers or the network. User setting: the audit checks HKEY_USERS\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\excel\security\fileblock:xl3macros (REG_DWORD) in every loaded user hive (S-1-5-21-*) and is compliant when each holds 2. It prints 'no-user-hive-loaded' (FAIL) when no user profile is loaded, so scan while users are logged on.
reference: CIS Microsoft Office Enterprise Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.2.4.7.2.2.5 Ensure 'Excel 3 macrosheets and add-in files' is set to 'Enabled: Open/Save blocked, use open policy'

audit.command: $sids = @(Get-ChildItem -Path 'Registry::HKEY_USERS' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -match '^S-1-5-21-\d+-\d+-\d+-\d+$' } | ForEach-Object { $_.PSChildName }); if ($sids.Count -eq 0) { 'no-user-hive-loaded' } else { $bad = @(); foreach ($s in $sids) { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path ('Registry::HKEY_USERS\' + $s + '\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\excel\security\fileblock') -Name 'xl3macros' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'xl3macros'; if (-not ($null -ne $v -and @(2) -contains [int64]$v)) { $bad += $s + ':xl3macros=' + $v } }; if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'non-compliant: ' + ($bad -join ', ') } }

remediation.guidance: Configure through Group Policy (User Configuration): User Configuration\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Excel 2016\Excel Options\Security\Trust Center\File Block Settings\Excel 3 Macrosheets and Add-in Files = Enabled: Open/Save blocked, use open policy

Rationale: If a file is saved with hidden markup, users might inadvertently distribute sensitive comments or information outside of their trusted circle without realizing that this information is still present in the document. User setting: the audit checks HKEY_USERS\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\word\options:showmarkupopensave (REG_DWORD) in every loaded user hive (S-1-5-21-*) and is compliant when each holds 1. It prints 'no-user-hive-loaded' (FAIL) when no user profile is loaded, so scan while users are logged on.
reference: CIS Microsoft Office Enterprise Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.11.8.7.3 Ensure 'Make hidden markup visible' is set to 'Enabled'

audit.command: $sids = @(Get-ChildItem -Path 'Registry::HKEY_USERS' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -match '^S-1-5-21-\d+-\d+-\d+-\d+$' } | ForEach-Object { $_.PSChildName }); if ($sids.Count -eq 0) { 'no-user-hive-loaded' } else { $bad = @(); foreach ($s in $sids) { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path ('Registry::HKEY_USERS\' + $s + '\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\word\options') -Name 'showmarkupopensave' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'showmarkupopensave'; if (-not ($null -ne $v -and @(1) -contains [int64]$v)) { $bad += $s + ':showmarkupopensave=' + $v } }; if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'non-compliant: ' + ($bad -join ', ') } }

remediation.guidance: Configure through Group Policy (User Configuration): User Configuration\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Word 2016\Word Options\Security\Make hidden markup visible = Enabled

title: Ensure OLE Package (Packager) object activation is blocked (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
description: Embedded OLE Package objects are used to deliver executables and scripts inside documents. PackagerPrompt 2 = block activation, 1 = prompt, 0 = run without prompt. Audit requires 2 under HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\<app>\security for word, excel and powerpoint. These Trust Center policies exist only in User Configuration (HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\...); there is no HKLM equivalent, so the audit evaluates the account running the scan. Run it as (or for) each interactive user, and enforce via User Configuration GPO/Intune.
reference: CIS Microsoft Office Benchmark - Security Settings: Packager object activation (PackagerPrompt)

audit.command: $bad = @(); foreach ($p in @('HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\word\security', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\excel\security', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\powerpoint\security')) { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name 'PackagerPrompt' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'PackagerPrompt'; if (-not (@('2') -contains "$v")) { $bad += "$(($p -split '\\')[6])=$v" } }; if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'non-compliant: ' + ($bad -join ', ') }

remediation.command: foreach ($p in @('HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\word\security', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\excel\security', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\powerpoint\security')) { if (-not (Test-Path -Path $p)) { New-Item -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name 'PackagerPrompt' -Value 2 -Type DWord }

title: Ensure 'Add-on Management' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting manages Internet Explorer add-ons — which add-ins are always enabled, always disabled (blocked), or configurable by the user. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled (Check: groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spDesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onent.exe, mse7.exe). Rationale: Internet Explorer add-ons are pieces of code that run in Internet Explorer to provide additional functionality. Rogue add-ons may contain viruses or other malicious code. Disabling or not configuring this setting could allow malicious code or users to become active on user computers or the network. 'Enabled: check all applications' writes one REG_DWORD 1 per Office executable under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Main\FeatureControl\FEATURE_ADDON_MANAGEMENT; the audit requires all 14 executables the ADMX writes (groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spdesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onenote.exe, mse7.exe) to be 1 and lists any that are missing or different.

title: Ensure 'Bind to object' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This setting determines whether Microsoft Internet Explorer performs its typical safety checks on Microsoft ActiveX® controls when opening URLs that are passed to it by an Office application. By default, Internet Explorer performs additional safety checks when ActiveX controls are initialized. Specifically, it prevents the control from being created if the kill bit is set in the registry. Rationale: Internet Explorer performs a number of safety checks before initializing an ActiveX control. It will not initialize a control if the kill bit for the control is set in the registry, or if the security settings for the zone in which the control is located do not allow it to be initialized. 'Enabled: check all applications' writes one REG_DWORD 1 per Office executable under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Main\FeatureControl\FEATURE_SAFE_BINDTOOBJECT; the audit requires all 14 executables the ADMX writes (groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spdesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onenote.exe, mse7.exe) to be 1 and lists any that are missing or different.

title: Ensure 'Consistent Mime Handling' is set to 'Enabled'
description: Internet Explorer uses Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) data to determine file handling procedures for files received through a Web server. This policy setting determines whether Internet Explorer requires all file-type information provided by Web servers to be consistent. Rationale: Users can use Internet Explorer to unknowingly download malicious content disguised with an incorrect filename extension or incorrectly marked in the MIME header. Once downloaded, an incorrect handler can run the file, enabling the malicious content to cause damage to the user's system or network. 'Enabled: check all applications' writes one REG_DWORD 1 per Office executable under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Main\FeatureControl\FEATURE_MIME_HANDLING; the audit requires all 14 executables the ADMX writes (groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spdesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onenote.exe, mse7.exe) to be 1 and lists any that are missing or different.

title: Ensure 'Disable user name and password' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This setting controls whether Internet Explorer opens URLs containing user information that are passed to it by an Office application. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled (Check: groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spDesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onent.exe, mse7.exe). Rationale: The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) standard allows user authentication to be included in URL strings in the form http://username:password@example.com. title: Ensure 'Local Machine Zone Lockdown Security' is set to 'Enabled'
description: When Internet Explorer opens a Web page, it places restrictions on what the page can do, based on the page's Internet Explorer security zone. description: This policy setting defines whether a reference to an object is accessible when the user navigates within the same domain or to a new domain. title: Ensure 'Protection From Zone Elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting prevents processes running in one zone from being elevated to higher privileges in another zone. Zone elevation attacks can be severe and happen relatively frequently. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled (Check: groove.exe, excel.exe, mspub.exe, powerpnt.exe, pptview.exe, visio.exe, winproj.exe, winword.exe, outlook.exe, spDesign.exe, exprwd.exe, msaccess.exe, onent.exe, mse7.exe). Rationale: Internet Explorer places restrictions on each web page that users can use the browser to open. Web pages on a user's local computer have the fewest security restrictions and reside in the Local Machine zone, making this security zone a prime target for malicious users and code. title: Ensure 'Restrict File Download' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting suppresses file download prompts that are not user-initiated. In certain circumstances, websites can initiate file download prompts without interaction from users. This technique can allow websites to put unauthorized files on users' hard drives if they click the wrong button and accept the download. Rationale: Disabling this setting allows websites to present file download prompts via code without the user specifically initiating the download. title: Ensure 'Enable Automatic Updates' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting controls whether the Office automatic updates are enabled or disabled for all Office products installed by using Click-to-Run. Note: This policy has no effect on Office products installed via Windows Installer. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled. Rationale: Security updates help prevent malicious attacks on Office applications. Timely application of Office updates helps ensure the security of devices and the applications running on the devices. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\officeupdate:enableautomaticupdates (REG_DWORD); compliant when it is 1. Remediation writes 1 locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.

title: Ensure 'Block Flash activation in Office documents' is set to 'Enabled: Block all activation'
description: This policy setting controls whether the Adobe Flash control can be activated by Office documents. Note that activation blocking applies only within Office processes. "Block all activation" prevents the Flash control from being loaded, whether directly referenced by the document or indirectly by another embedded object. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: Block all activation. Rationale: Adobe Flash was discontinued in 2020. Flash content has had a long history of exploitation by malicious software developers. Blocking will ensure Office does not execute any Flash content. Enforcing the default ensures that the system was not configured in an insecure way. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. The MS Security Guide template records the chosen option as the string 'Block all Flash activation' in HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\Common\COM Compatibility:Comment.

title: Ensure 'Restrict legacy JScript execution for Office' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting controls JScript execution per Security Zone within Internet Explorer and WebBrowser Control (WebOC) for Office applications. JScript is Microsoft's legacy dialect of the ECMAScript standard that is used in Microsoft's Internet Explorer 11 and older. Rationale: Development on the JScript engine ended, and the component was deprecated with the release of Internet Explorer 8.0 in 2009, but the engine remained in all Windows OS versions as a legacy component inside IE. Due to this, it has been exploited by bad actors over the years, including nation-states. title: Ensure 'Disable all trusted locations' is set to 'Enabled'
description: This policy setting allows administrators to disable all trusted locations in the specified applications. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled. Rationale: Trusted locations specified in the Trust Center are used to define file locations that are assumed to be safe. Content, code, and add-ins are allowed to load from trusted locations with a minimal amount of security, without prompting the users for permission. User setting: the audit checks HKEY_USERS\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\access\security\trustedlocations:alllocationsdisabled (REG_DWORD) in every loaded user hive (S-1-5-21-*) and is compliant when each holds 1. The recommended state for this setting is: Disabled. Rationale: The Windows Rights Management Add-on for Internet Explorer provides a way for users who do not use the Office release to view, but not alter, files with restricted permissions. By default, IRM-enabled files are saved in a format that cannot be viewed by using the Windows Rights Management Add-on. User setting: the audit checks HKEY_USERS\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\drm:includehtml (REG_DWORD) in every loaded user hive (S-1-5-21-*) and is compliant when each holds 0. It prints 'no-user-hive-loaded' (FAIL) when no user profile is loaded, so scan while users are logged on.
reference: CIS Microsoft Office Enterprise Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.3.18.1 Ensure 'Allow users with earlier versions of Office to read with browsers...' is set to 'Disabled'
